name: Masseria Torre Maizza, A Rocco Forte Hotel

seo.title: Masseria Torre Maizza: Rocco Forte Puglia Honeymoon Review
seo.description: Sun-drenched Rocco Forte masseria with golf and beach club. Score 88/100, from $750/night. Verdict, suite pick, 7-night itinerary.

content.verdict: Masseria Torre Maizza is the Rocco Forte family’s Puglian masseria — a 16th-century watchtower-and-farmhouse complex on a 300-acre olive estate at Savelletri di Fasano, between Borgo Egnazia and Masseria San Domenico, reimagined by Olga Polizzi (Sir Rocco Forte’s sister and the group’s design director) in 2019 with the sun-drenched palette of yellows, terracottas, and indigo blues that has become the visual signature of the hotel. Forty rooms only — substantially more intimate than Borgo Egnazia’s 184 — across the converted main masseria, the surrounding limonaia and stables, and a small number of private garden suites. The five-acre formal Italian garden with its central infinity pool, the 9-hole pitch-and-putt golf course, the Maizza Spa (with hammam, indoor pool, and 8 treatment rooms), and the private beach club at Coccaro Beach Club (200m away, on the Adriatic) make this a full-amenity luxury masseria at half the scale of Borgo Egnazia. The food is excellent: Carosello on the panoramic terrace is the destination restaurant under chef Gennaro Russo (creative Puglian cooking, no Michelin star but at-star level), Trullo for casual lunches, and the Beach Club for grilled fish on the sand. The honeymoon move is one of the Pizzica Suites — the largest suite category, with private terrace, a private garden, and outdoor shower — or the Limonaia Suite in the converted lemon house with its 18th-century stone vault. The defining moment: aperitivo on the rooftop of the original 16th-century watchtower (which now houses a small library and a wood-fired pizza terrace) at sunset, with the olive groves stretching to the Adriatic. Caveats: still a resort with 40 keys rather than a 10-room boutique; the immediate area on the SS379 coastal road outside is not picturesque; and Rocco Forte service is excellent but more formal-corporate than the warm family welcome at smaller masserias. But for honeymooners who want full luxury amenity (spa, pool, beach club, golf, fine dining) at a more intimate 40-key scale than Borgo Egnazia, Torre Maizza is the clear pick.
content.best_room: A Pizzica Suite — private terrace, private garden, outdoor shower, the largest suite category. For something more historic, the Limonaia Suite in the converted lemon house with its 18th-century stone vault. Avoid the standard Tarantata rooms in the main building — lovely but smaller and without the private outdoor space that defines a Puglian honeymoon.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Arrival and Carosello dinner
itinerary_7_nights.description: Drive 30 minutes from Brindisi. Check-in to your Pizzica Suite, welcome Spumante. Aperitivo on the watchtower rooftop. Dinner at Carosello on the panoramic terrace.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Coccaro Beach Club
itinerary_7_nights.description: Shuttle to Coccaro Beach Club (5 min). Full morning on the Adriatic. Lunch at the beach restaurant — grilled total fish, Verdeca white. Return for the spa. Dinner at Trullo.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Itria Valley white towns
itinerary_7_nights.description: Driver-and-guide to Locorotondo and Cisternino. Long lunch at Trullo Sovrano in Alberobello. Return for the pool. Dinner at Carosello.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Lecce baroque day
itinerary_7_nights.description: Driver to Lecce (1h). Private baroque walking tour. Lunch at Bros’ (1 Michelin star). Return via the Salento coast. Spa evening.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Slow masseria day
itinerary_7_nights.description: Long breakfast on your terrace. Cooking class with the kitchen team — orecchiette and burrata. Lunch with your pasta. Afternoon golf on the 9-hole course. Casual dinner at Trullo.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Polignano a Mare
itinerary_7_nights.description: Driver north to Polignano. Lunch at Grotta Palazzese (the sea-cave restaurant) at noon. Afternoon swim at Cala Porto. Final dinner at Carosello.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Slow departure
itinerary_7_nights.description: Final breakfast on the terrace. Drive to Brindisi for departure.

caveats: Still a 40-key resort rather than a 10-room boutique. Masseria Le Carrube is more intimate.
The SS379 coastal road immediately outside is not picturesque. Stay on-property and use the shuttle.
Rocco Forte service is excellent but more formally corporate than smaller family masserias.

faqs.question: Good for honeymooners?
faqs.answer: Among the top Puglian honeymoons — full amenity (spa, pool, beach, golf, dining) at 40-key intimacy. The Pizzica Suites with private gardens are exceptional.

faqs.question: Best time to visit?
faqs.answer: May, June and September are ideal. October still excellent. Closed late November to late March.

faqs.question: Book in advance?
faqs.answer: Pizzica and Limonaia Suites 6–9 months for May–September. Standard rooms 4 months. August requires 9+ months.

faqs.question: Adults-only?
faqs.answer: No — Rocco Forte properties globally are family-friendly. Expect some families in school holidays. The Pizzica Suites with private gardens give honeymoon privacy.

faqs.question: Best room type?
faqs.answer: Pizzica Suite for the private garden. Limonaia Suite for the historic vaulted interior. Avoid standard Tarantata rooms.

faqs.question: How to get there?
faqs.answer: Brindisi (BDS) is 30 minutes by car. Bari (BRI) 60 minutes. Hire car at airport, or hotel chauffeur €150 from BDS.
